readings.title: The repair remembered
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: When the North Quay archive collected memories of an old ferry, several residents described a dramatic rescue. One retired mechanic instead spoke about an ordinary repair. He explained how workers borrowed tools from a nearby bakery after a handle broke. The interviewer almost omitted this account because nothing dangerous had happened. Later, a teacher used it to discuss cooperation between local businesses. Students asked why such practical relationships rarely appeared in official reports. The archive then added a search term for everyday work. Its curator concluded that an event need not be spectacular to reveal how a community functioned.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: A room that changed the sound
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A language centre purchased excellent microphones, yet recordings from its meeting room sounded unclear. Staff first blamed the equipment. An audio technician noticed that speech bounced between bare walls, creating echoes. Instead of recommending another purchase, she hung temporary curtains and placed a rug on the floor. The next recording was easier to understand even though the microphone settings stayed the same. The centre kept the curtains but chose a washable floor covering for daily use. Its experience showed that better results can come from changing the surroundings of a tool, rather than the tool itself.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: Permission after an interview
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Before being interviewed, Mara agreed that her words could be used in a small research class. Months later, the interviewer was invited to post the recording on a public website. He contacted her again rather than treating the first agreement as unlimited. Mara welcomed wider access but asked him to remove a section about a former colleague. They prepared an edited version and attached a note explaining that some material was omitted at the speaker's request. The note did not reveal the missing details. The researcher believed openness about editing could coexist with respect for a contributor's boundaries.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The useful imperfect transcript
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Volunteers at a sound archive tested automatic transcripts of market interviews. The software handled clear speech well but confused unfamiliar stall names. Rather than correcting every hesitation first, volunteers marked names, prices and place references for careful checking. They kept a link from each paragraph to the corresponding audio. Visitors could therefore listen when a wording seemed doubtful. A sign described the transcript as a guide, not a replacement for the recording. After a month, users reported fewer serious misunderstandings. The team had improved usefulness by concentrating effort on errors that could change a listener's understanding.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into Chinese.

A voice recording carries more than the words a person chooses. A pause may suggest uncertainty, while laughter can change the meaning of an ordinary sentence. Written transcripts help people locate information, but they cannot preserve every feature of speech. Keeping the original sound allows future listeners to ask questions that today's editors have not considered.
translation.referenceAnswer: 声音录音承载的不只是一个人选择的词语。停顿可能暗示不确定，而笑声会改变一句普通话语的意思。文字稿有助于人们查找信息，却无法保留口语的所有特征。保存原始声音，使未来的听众能够提出今天的编辑尚未考虑过的问题。
translation.explanation: 参考译文展示一种可接受的表达；保留原文信息及逻辑、中文通顺的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 English words for this original simulation task.

Your town archive wants short recordings from residents. Write an invitation explaining the purpose, suggesting one kind of experience to share, and describing how contributors can choose whether their names appear.
writing.sampleAnswer: Our town archive invites residents to record a memory of everyday life. We hope to show how people worked, travelled and helped one another, including experiences that seldom appear in official documents. You might describe a journey to your first job or explain how your street prepared for a local celebration. A clear story matters more than a polished speaking style. Before recording, a volunteer will explain where the material may be used. You can choose to be named, use a different name or remain unnamed in the public collection. We will discuss any sensitive passages with you before publication. Please contact the archive desk to arrange a convenient time.
writing.explanation: 范文用于作答后参考；观点与例子可以不同，但须回应全部要求并表达清楚。

criteria.name: 语言表达
criteria.description: 用词准确，句式基本正确；根据错误对表达和理解的影响扣分。
